_readme: Approximate coordinates for plotting Lonesome Dove (1985 novel). The novel's geography is loose and often compresses distances; coordinates are best-fit real-world anchors, not canon. 'confidence' reflects how firmly the TEXT pins the place (high = named real place; medium = named but vague, e.g. an unnamed crossing of a named river; low = inferred or fictional). Lat/lon in decimal degrees (WGS84). Chapter numbers refer to the novel's numbering (102 chapters).

cattleDrive.description: Hat Creek Cattle Company herd, Lonesome Dove, Texas to the Milk River, Montana Territory. Leaves about the first of April (ch 12, 19, 25); reaches the Milk River in autumn and winters there (ch 98).

points.name: Lonesome Dove (Hat Creek Cattle Company)
points.realWorld: Fictional border town on the north bank of the Rio Grande in the south Texas brush country; best fit is the Rio Grande between Eagle Pass and Laredo (Coahuila lies across the river)
points.notes: Hat Creek is a dry sandy ditch through town. The old Comanche crossing is about a mile upriver (west).

points.name: Old Comanche crossing (near a salt lick)
points.realWorld: Rio Grande about a mile above (west of) Lonesome Dove

points.name: Hacienda Flores (raid target)
points.realWorld: Fictional; 'largest ranch in Coahuila', about 30 miles southeast of Lonesome Dove across the Rio Grande
points.notes: Side trip, not part of the drive. Burnt-out out camp where the O'Briens are found is a few miles from it.

points.name: Sabinas, Coahuila (Gus's detour)
points.realWorld: Sabinas, Coahuila, Mexico
points.notes: Named; Gus steals saddles and horses from drunk bandits there on the way back (ch 12). Real Sabinas is further than the novel implies.

points.name: Herd gathered and held in a valley ~5 miles from Lonesome Dove
points.realWorld: Near the Rio Grande outside town

points.name: Brush country (mesquite thickets) south of the Nueces
points.realWorld: South Texas brush country between the Rio Grande and the Nueces
points.notes: Sandstorm, then lightning storm scatter the herd (ch 31).

points.name: Nueces River crossing (Sean O'Brien killed by water moccasins; buried under an oak)
points.realWorld: Nueces River, likely between Crystal City and Cotulla, Texas
points.notes: River named; crossing point not named. First river of the drive.

points.name: San Antonio River crossing
points.realWorld: San Antonio River south/southeast of San Antonio, Texas

points.name: Wagon wreck at a little creek; Bolivar quits
points.realWorld: Creek just south of San Antonio

points.name: San Antonio (Buckhorn saloon, the Alamo, new wagon bought)
points.realWorld: San Antonio, Texas
points.notes: Call and Gus ride in; the herd skirts the town.

points.name: Clara's orchard (spring-fed creek and live-oak grove on a Guadalupe tributary)
points.realWorld: Texas Hill Country on or near the Guadalupe River between San Antonio and Austin; ch 96 calls it 'the south Guadalupe'
points.notes: Where Gus proposed to Clara; Gus's burial place (ch 102). The text is inconsistent: ch 44 puts it off the route toward Austin, ch 96 says the south Guadalupe (the South Fork of the Guadalupe is near Hunt/Kerrville, ~30.07,-99.33 — alternative placement).

points.name: Herd camp ~20 miles west of Austin; Jake and Lorena's camp under a limestone bluff (Blue Duck visits; Lorena abducted)
points.realWorld: Hill Country west of Austin, Texas (around Dripping Springs)

points.name: Austin (Call looks for a cook; Po Campo hired)
points.realWorld: Austin, Texas
points.notes: Clara's parents' store was here (memory, ch 7).

points.name: Brazos River crossing
points.realWorld: Brazos River between Austin and Fort Worth (crossing unnamed)

points.name: Trinity River crossing; herd held west of Fort Worth
points.realWorld: West of Fort Worth, Texas
points.notes: Hands visit Fort Worth and see Jake gambling (ch 59, 64).

points.name: Red River crossing (at a gravel bar; point unnamed) into Indian Territory
points.realWorld: Red River, Texas/Oklahoma. Unnamed in the text; a later route via the Canadian near Adobe Walls and the Arkansas west of Dodge fits the Western Trail crossing at Doan's (34.35,-99.26). The Chisholm Trail's Red River Station (33.88,-97.73) is the alternative.

points.name: Lightning kills Bill Spettle; Canadian River crossing in hail
points.realWorld: Canadian River in Indian Territory (western Oklahoma), probably near the Western Trail crossing
points.notes: Gus and Lorena rejoin just north of the Canadian (ch 62-63).

points.name: South edge of Kansas: grasshopper swarm; turn west for water

points.realWorld: Unnamed creek on the Kansas prairie, north of the Arkansas and east of the herd

points.name: Republican River crossing
points.realWorld: Republican River near the Kansas/Nebraska line

points.name: Stinking Water crossing

points.realWorld: On the Platte about 20 miles from Ogallala; the text leans west of town (Weaver, ch 83), so near Brule/Big Springs, Nebraska
points.notes: Jake in ch 7 says 'on the North Platte', but later chapters just say the Platte near Ogallala (which is on the South Platte).

points.name: Leave the Platte where it bends south toward Colorado; ~80 waterless miles into Wyoming
points.realWorld: South Platte near Julesburg, Colorado, heading northwest
points.notes: Real distance to Salt Creek is far more than 80 miles; the novel compresses.

points.name: Salt Creek (end of the dry drive; two days' rest; horses stolen)
points.realWorld: Salt Creek, Wyoming (tributary of the Powder River)
points.notes: GradeSaver/Shmoop call it 'Salt River'; the text says Salt Creek.

points.name: Powder River; then Crazy Woman Creek (grizzly fights the Texas bull on a branch of it)

points.name: Yellowstone River crossing (near Miles City)

points.realWorld: Musselshell River country, central Montana (the novel's distances to Miles City don't fit the real river well)
points.notes: Hugh Auld says the attackers were Bloods; TheBestNotes says Utes (not in the text).

points.name: Miles City (Gus's leg amputated; dies; body stored in Dr. Mobley's harness shed)
points.realWorld: Miles City, Montana

points.name: Missouri River crossing near Fort Benton (Army buys 200 head; Jasper nearly drowns)
points.realWorld: Fort Benton, Montana

points.name: Marais (Marias) River crossing; Old Dog the lead steer killed by grizzlies

points.name: Milk River (Canada just north, per Hugh Auld)
points.realWorld: Milk River, north-central Montana

points.realWorld: North-central Montana, roughly between Havre and the Missouri Breaks
points.notes: End of the drive. Fort Buford (Call's beef deliveries) is at 47.98,-104.0.
